purpose: Evaluate orientation, phyllary posture and involucre stickiness in one trait-blind nine-variable present-environment universe using the same occurrence/QC rules.

occurrence.role: provenance frame matching Japan38 nuclear tips; not a biological region class

inference.primary: nine-dimensional standardized omnibus finite state-label permutation rank within each trait
inference.secondary: all nine univariate two-sided exact ranks; Benjamini-Hochberg across all evaluable trait x environment rows
inference.no_borrowed_direction: Do not transfer the orientation-specific BIO15/BIO1 sign hypothesis to phyllary or stickiness.
inference.coverage_rule: A state represented by one taxon remains lineage-confounded; lowering the occurrence gate does not create biological replication.

claim_ceiling: Present-environment correspondence is not adaptation, selection or historical cause.
The nine-variable atlas is exploratory across traits; single-axis leads must be reported with the full multiplicity context.
Taxon-level authority states are not measured at each occurrence coordinate.
Japan is a provenance frame matching the Japan38 phylogeny, not a biological region class.
Phyllary coverage failure, if retained, is a resolution result rather than evidence of no ecology.
